I found no convention violations that block this PR, and I didn't run the Level 1 or Level 2 zoom on any rule. I worked through all 78 rules in the generated checklist against `git diff 3f9918c6a…HEAD`, which touches 3 files: `transaction-guards.ts`, its test, and `MigrateSafeL2Review.tsx`. Nothing was modified, installed or run apart from the checklist script.

## Findings report

| # | Severity | Rule | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Low | CODE / comments (AGENTS.md "treat comments as tech debt") | `apps/web/src/utils/safe-migrations.ts:101-106` | The JSDoc on `isSafeMigrationCall` still says it is used only "to avoid flagging the migration tx itself as an unsupported-contract interaction". This PR also makes it the check for "is this a version upgrade" at `transaction-guards.ts:452`, so the comment is now incomplete. Suggest describing what the function detects rather than who calls it. |
| 2 | Low / nit | TEST-05 (builders for unit tests) | `apps/web/src/utils/__tests__/transaction-guards.test.ts:205`, `:220` | Both new tests build `TransactionData` as hand-written object literals, although `txDataBuilder` is already imported in this file. This matches the neighbouring `1.3.0+ migrations` test, so it is consistent locally, but it doesn't follow the rule's preferred `Builder` pattern. It doesn't break the rule's actual check, since there are no MSW fixture imports. |
| 3 | Info | TEST-02 (tests for new branches) | `apps/web/src/utils/transaction-guards.ts:450-452` | Only canonical addresses are tested through `isSafeUpdateTxData`. The zksync variant (e.g. `0x817756C6…` for 1.4.1) is newly matched here and has no test at this level; it relies on the direct `isSafeMigrationCall` tests in `safe-migrations.test.ts`. That's acceptable; an extra zksync case would pin the behaviour to this caller. |
| 4 | Info | CHAIN-01 | `apps/web/src/utils/transaction-guards.ts:452` | The check now uses real deployment data instead of the hardcoded `LATEST_SAFE_VERSION`. That is what CHAIN-01 and CHAIN-03 ask for. It ignores chain ID and matches official addresses from every version and variant. That's fine because the code first requires `trustedDelegateCallTarget` and a delegate call, but it is a deliberate widening. |
| 5 | Info | TEST-01 | `apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/flows/MigrateSafeL2/MigrateSafeL2Review.tsx:26-36` | Removing the wrapper `<div>` is a layout-only fix and has no test. That's reasonable for a CSS `:first-child` fix, but it's worth a screenshot in the PR's visual summary, as AGENTS.md requires. |

## Rules that applied

- **DATA-05:** pass. Addresses are compared with `sameAddress`.
- **TEST-01:** pass. The 1.5.0 test would fail if the hardcoded single-version check came back. The `0xdeadbeef` negative test would fail if the selector check were removed. I confirmed the fixtures are real: `0x6439e7AB…` is the canonical 1.5.0 SafeMigration address and `0x68cb3d94` is the `migrateL2WithFallbackHandler()` selector. I checked these against safe-deployments 1.37.63 in another local checkout, because this worktree has no `node_modules`.
- **TEST-02:** mostly passes (see #3).
- **TEST-05:** the check passes; the preference for builders is not followed (see #2).
- **API-01:** not affected. Only two imports were removed, and no exports changed.
- **REVIEW-01 / PROD-01:** not applicable. This is a fix PR, not an infra PR, and the layout change is explained in the commit message.

All other rules didn't apply to this diff. I marked all 78 items as checked in `docs/engineering/pr-self-review-checklist.generated.md`. `git check-ignore` reports that file as not ignored, contrary to the skill's `.gitignore` requirement, but `docs/engineering/` is entirely untracked, so no tracked file changed.
